description: Triage a security alert in a SOC from initial receipt through context gathering, classification, and disposition.

steps.description: Receive and categorize an incoming security alert by source, type, and initial severity.

inputs.name: alert-data
inputs.desc: Raw alert from SIEM, EDR, or other detection source

inputs.name: alert-source
inputs.desc: Name of the system that generated the alert

outputs.name: classified-alert
outputs.desc: Alert with category, type, and initial severity assigned

outputs.name: alert-timeline
outputs.desc: Timestamp sequence of alert-related events

process: Parse the alert payload and extract key fields (source IP, destination, user, process, rule name)
Categorize by type: malware, intrusion, policy violation, anomaly, or data loss
Assign initial severity based on the detection rule's priority and asset criticality

steps.description: Gather contextual information about the assets, users, and threat intelligence related to the alert.

inputs.name: classified-alert
inputs.desc: Alert with category and initial severity

outputs.name: enriched-alert
outputs.desc: Alert enriched with asset, user, and threat intel context

outputs.name: related-alerts
outputs.desc: List of correlated alerts from the same timeframe or assets

process: Query the asset inventory for the affected system's owner, criticality, and network zone
Look up user activity in the identity provider and recent authentication logs
Check threat intelligence feeds for indicators mentioned in the alert
Search for related alerts on the same asset or user within the past 24 hours

steps.description: Determine whether the alert is a true positive, false positive, or requires further investigation.

inputs.name: enriched-alert
inputs.desc: Alert with full context from asset, user, and threat intel lookups

inputs.name: related-alerts
inputs.desc: Correlated alerts from the same timeframe or assets

outputs.name: tp-fp-determination
outputs.desc: Classification as true positive, false positive, or needs investigation

outputs.name: determination-evidence
outputs.desc: Evidence supporting the true/false positive classification

process: Compare the alert indicators against known benign activity baselines for the asset
Check if the activity matches a known attack pattern or technique
Evaluate whether the context (user behavior, time of day, business process) explains the activity
Classify as true positive, false positive, or indeterminate requiring deeper investigation

steps.description: Assess the severity and scope of a confirmed true positive alert.

inputs.name: tp-fp-determination
inputs.desc: Classification of the alert as true positive

outputs.name: severity-assessment
outputs.desc: Final severity rating with justification

outputs.name: scope-assessment
outputs.desc: Number of affected systems, users, and data types

process: Determine the number of affected systems by searching for the same indicators across the environment
Assess data exposure risk based on the type of system and data classification
Rate final severity (critical, high, medium, low) factoring in asset criticality, data sensitivity, and blast radius

steps.description: Route the alert to the appropriate team for escalation or close it with documentation.

inputs.name: scope-assessment
inputs.desc: Affected systems, users, and data types

outputs.name: escalation-decision
outputs.desc: Decision to escalate, contain, or close with routing details

outputs.name: notification-list
outputs.desc: List of teams and individuals to notify

process: Apply the escalation matrix to determine the required response level
Identify the responsible team (tier 2 analyst, incident response, management) based on severity and type
Prepare the notification with a summary of findings, severity, and recommended next steps

steps.description: Produce the triage decision record documenting the alert, analysis, and disposition.

inputs.name: escalation-decision
inputs.desc: Decision to escalate, contain, or close

outputs.name: triage-record
outputs.desc: Complete triage decision record with timeline, evidence, and disposition

outputs.name: metrics-data
outputs.desc: Triage timing and outcome data for SOC metrics

process: Compile the full timeline from alert receipt through disposition
Document the evidence chain: what was checked, what was found, what was concluded
Record the disposition (escalated, closed as false positive, closed as handled) with rationale
Calculate triage time for SOC performance metrics

description: Plan and execute a proactive threat hunting campaign from hypothesis through detection rule creation.

steps.description: Select a threat hunting hypothesis based on threat intelligence, detection gaps, or emerging attack techniques.

inputs.name: threat-landscape
inputs.desc: Current threat intelligence reports and advisories

inputs.name: detection-coverage-map
inputs.desc: Map of MITRE ATT&CK techniques with current detection status

outputs.name: hunt-hypothesis
outputs.desc: Specific hypothesis to test, including the expected attacker behavior

outputs.name: attack-technique-profile
outputs.desc: Detailed description of the technique including data sources and artifacts

process: Review recent threat intelligence for techniques targeting your industry or technology stack
Identify gaps in the ATT&CK coverage map where no detection exists
Select the hypothesis that balances likelihood of occurrence with potential impact
Document the expected attacker behavior, artifacts, and data sources

steps.description: Define the data sources, queries, and tools needed to test the hunting hypothesis.

inputs.name: attack-technique-profile
inputs.desc: Expected artifacts and data sources for the technique

outputs.name: hunt-plan
outputs.desc: Detailed plan with data sources, queries, and analysis procedures

outputs.name: query-library
outputs.desc: Collection of queries for each data source to execute during the hunt

process: Map the technique artifacts to available log sources (endpoint, network, identity, cloud)
Write queries for each data source to surface the expected behavior patterns
Define the analysis workflow: what to look for in query results and how to pivot

steps.description: Execute the hunt queries across the environment and collect results.

inputs.name: hunt-plan
inputs.desc: Plan with data sources and analysis procedures

inputs.name: query-library
inputs.desc: Queries to execute against each data source

outputs.name: raw-hunt-results
outputs.desc: Query results from all data sources

outputs.name: execution-log
outputs.desc: Log of queries run, time ranges covered, and data volumes processed

process: Execute each query against the specified data sources and time ranges
Record the results with timestamps, affected systems, and users
Note any data gaps (missing log sources, retention issues) that limit the hunt

steps.description: Analyze the hunt results to identify anomalies, suspicious patterns, and potential threats.

inputs.name: raw-hunt-results
inputs.desc: Query results from all data sources

inputs.name: execution-log
inputs.desc: Log of queries and data coverage

outputs.name: findings-list
outputs.desc: List of anomalies and suspicious patterns with supporting evidence

outputs.name: false-positive-notes
outputs.desc: Benign explanations identified during analysis for future reference

process: Filter results to remove known benign activity and approved exceptions
Group remaining results by pattern: same technique, same actor, or same target
Investigate each group to determine if it represents a real threat or a benign anomaly
Document false positive patterns for future hunt refinement

steps.description: Create detection rules from confirmed findings and validated patterns.

inputs.name: false-positive-notes
inputs.desc: Known benign patterns to exclude in detection rules

outputs.name: new-detection-rules
outputs.desc: Detection rules (Sigma, YARA, or SIEM-native) created from hunt findings

outputs.name: coverage-update
outputs.desc: Updated ATT&CK coverage map reflecting new detections

process: For each confirmed finding, write a detection rule that captures the malicious pattern
Add exclusions for the documented false positive patterns
Test the rule against historical data to validate detection rate and false positive rate
Update the ATT&CK coverage map with the new detections

steps.description: Produce the hunt campaign report documenting hypothesis, methods, findings, and new detections.

inputs.name: new-detection-rules
inputs.desc: Detection rules created from the hunt

outputs.name: hunt-report
outputs.desc: Complete threat hunting report with findings, detections, and recommendations

outputs.name: hunt-metrics
outputs.desc: Campaign metrics: time spent, data analyzed, findings count, detections created

process: Summarize the hypothesis, the data sources searched, and the time ranges covered
Document each finding with evidence, severity assessment, and remediation action taken
List new detection rules with their expected coverage and false positive baselines
Calculate campaign metrics for the threat hunting program

description: Develop and validate YARA rules for malware detection from sample analysis through production deployment.

steps.description: Analyze malware samples to identify unique byte patterns, strings, and structural features.

inputs.name: malware-samples
inputs.desc: Collection of malware samples to build detection for

inputs.name: malware-family-info
inputs.desc: Known information about the malware family and variants

outputs.name: unique-indicators
outputs.desc: List of unique strings, byte patterns, and structural features

outputs.name: sample-analysis-notes
outputs.desc: Analysis notes on packing, obfuscation, and variant differences

process: Extract strings, imports, and section headers from each sample
Identify byte patterns that appear across all samples in the family but are rare in benign software
Note any packing or obfuscation that may affect pattern stability across variants
Rank indicators by uniqueness and stability

steps.description: Select the best patterns and conditions for the YARA rule based on uniqueness and stability.

inputs.name: unique-indicators
inputs.desc: Candidate strings, byte patterns, and structural features

inputs.name: sample-analysis-notes
inputs.desc: Notes on packing, obfuscation, and variants

outputs.name: selected-patterns
outputs.desc: Final set of patterns chosen for the rule

outputs.name: condition-logic
outputs.desc: Boolean condition combining the patterns

process: Select patterns that are present in all known samples and absent from a reference benign corpus
Choose a mix of string and byte patterns for resilience against minor variants
Design the condition logic: require N of M patterns to balance detection rate and specificity

steps.description: Write the YARA rule with proper metadata, strings section, and condition.

outputs.name: draft-yara-rule
outputs.desc: Complete YARA rule with metadata, strings, and condition

outputs.name: rule-documentation
outputs.desc: Documentation of what the rule detects and known limitations

process: Write the rule metadata (author, description, date, reference, severity)
Define the strings section with hex patterns, text strings, and regex where needed
Write the condition combining patterns with file size, header, or section constraints
Document the rule's intended target, known limitations, and expected false positive rate

steps.description: Test the YARA rule against a known-good corpus to measure the false positive rate.

inputs.name: rule-documentation
inputs.desc: Documentation of the rule's intended target

outputs.name: fp-test-results
outputs.desc: False positive count and list of matching benign files

outputs.name: fp-analysis
outputs.desc: Analysis of why each false positive matched and how to fix it

process: Scan the known-good corpus (system files, common applications, documents) with the rule
Record every match and inspect why the benign file triggered the rule
Classify each false positive by cause: coincidental string match, common library code, or rule too broad

steps.description: Test the YARA rule against a malware corpus to measure the true positive detection rate.

outputs.name: detection-rate
outputs.desc: Percentage of target malware samples detected

outputs.name: missed-samples
outputs.desc: List of malware samples not detected with analysis of why

process: Scan the full malware corpus (target family plus related variants) with the rule
Calculate the detection rate: matches divided by total target samples
Analyze missed samples to determine if they are heavily packed, newer variants, or outliers

steps.description: Optimize the YARA rule to reduce false positives and improve detection rate.

outputs.name: optimized-yara-rule
outputs.desc: Refined YARA rule with improved precision and recall

outputs.name: optimization-changelog
outputs.desc: Record of changes made and their impact on detection metrics

process: Tighten patterns that caused false positives by adding context or constraints
Add alternative patterns to catch missed variants without broadening too much
Re-test against both corpora to verify improvement
Document every change and its effect on detection rate and false positive rate

steps.description: Produce the validated YARA rule package with documentation and test results.

inputs.name: optimization-changelog
inputs.desc: Record of changes and metric impacts

outputs.name: validated-rule-package
outputs.desc: Production-ready YARA rule with metadata and documentation

outputs.name: validation-report
outputs.desc: Full report with detection rate, false positive rate, and test methodology

process: Package the final rule with complete metadata fields
Write the validation report: test methodology, corpus sizes, detection rate, false positive rate
Include deployment guidance: which scanning platforms, recommended scan frequency, alert priority

description: Develop and validate Sigma detection rules from technique identification through SIEM deployment.

steps.description: Research the attack technique to detect, including log artifacts and observable behaviors.

inputs.name: technique-id
inputs.desc: MITRE ATT&CK technique ID or description of the behavior to detect

inputs.name: environment-context
inputs.desc: Technology stack and log sources available in the environment

outputs.name: technique-profile
outputs.desc: Detailed profile of the technique including tools, procedures, and artifacts

outputs.name: log-source-mapping
outputs.desc: Map of which log sources capture which artifacts of the technique

process: Research the technique in ATT&CK, threat reports, and red team documentation
Identify the specific log events and fields that capture the technique's artifacts
Determine which log sources in the environment can observe these events
Note variations in how different tools and procedures execute the same technique

steps.description: Write the Sigma rule with proper taxonomy, log source definition, and detection logic.

inputs.name: technique-profile
inputs.desc: Technique details including artifacts and procedures

inputs.name: log-source-mapping
inputs.desc: Available log sources and their relevant fields

outputs.name: draft-sigma-rule
outputs.desc: Sigma rule in YAML format with title, description, logsource, detection, and level

outputs.name: rule-metadata
outputs.desc: ATT&CK mapping, references, and author information

process: Define the logsource category, product, and service fields per Sigma taxonomy
Write the detection section with selection criteria and filter conditions
Set the level (informational, low, medium, high, critical) based on technique severity and confidence
Add ATT&CK tags, references, and false positive documentation

steps.description: Convert the Sigma rule to the target SIEM query language for testing.

outputs.name: siem-query
outputs.desc: Rule converted to the target SIEM format (Splunk SPL, Elastic KQL, etc.)

outputs.name: conversion-notes
outputs.desc: Notes on any field mappings or adjustments needed for the target SIEM

process: Run the Sigma rule through the converter for the target SIEM platform
Review the converted query for correctness, especially field name mappings
Adjust for any platform-specific syntax or field naming conventions

steps.description: Test the rule against labeled datasets containing both attack and benign activity.

outputs.name: test-results
outputs.desc: Detection rate on attack data and false positive rate on benign data

outputs.name: sample-matches
outputs.desc: Example matches from both attack and benign datasets

process: Run the query against a dataset of known attack activity to measure detection rate
Run the query against a dataset of normal business activity to measure false positive rate
Inspect sample matches to verify the rule triggers on the expected events

steps.description: Tune the rule to reduce false positives while maintaining detection coverage.

inputs.name: test-results
inputs.desc: Detection rate and false positive rate

outputs.name: tuned-sigma-rule
outputs.desc: Refined Sigma rule with improved precision

outputs.name: tuning-changelog
outputs.desc: Record of filter additions and their impact on metrics

process: Analyze false positive matches to identify common benign patterns
Add filter conditions to exclude the identified benign patterns
Re-test to verify false positives decreased without reducing true positive detection
Document each filter addition and its impact

steps.description: Produce the validated Sigma rule with test results and deployment documentation.

inputs.name: tuning-changelog
inputs.desc: Record of changes and metric impacts

outputs.name: validated-sigma-rule
outputs.desc: Production-ready Sigma rule with complete metadata

outputs.name: sigma-validation-report
outputs.desc: Test results, tuning history, and deployment guidance

process: Finalize the rule with complete metadata, references, and false positive documentation
Write the validation report: test methodology, dataset sizes, final detection and FP rates
Include deployment guidance: recommended SIEM configuration, alert routing, and response procedure

description: Build a security detection from coverage gap identification through production deployment and monitoring.

steps.description: Identify gaps in detection coverage by mapping existing detections to the MITRE ATT&CK framework.

inputs.name: current-detection-inventory
inputs.desc: List of all active detection rules with their ATT&CK mappings

inputs.name: threat-priority-list
inputs.desc: Prioritized list of threat actors and techniques relevant to the environment

outputs.name: coverage-gaps
outputs.desc: List of ATT&CK techniques with no detection or weak detection

outputs.name: gap-priority-ranking
outputs.desc: Gaps ranked by threat relevance and exploitability

process: Map each existing detection rule to ATT&CK technique IDs
Overlay the threat priority list to identify high-risk techniques with no coverage
Rank gaps by the product of threat likelihood and detection difficulty
Select the top gap to build a detection for

steps.description: Research the data requirements for detecting the target technique.

inputs.name: gap-priority-ranking
inputs.desc: Priority context for the selected technique

outputs.name: data-requirements
outputs.desc: Required log sources, fields, and retention for the detection

outputs.name: data-availability-assessment
outputs.desc: Assessment of which required data is available and any gaps

process: Identify every log source that can observe the technique's artifacts
Check which of those sources are currently collected and at what retention
Document any data gaps that would need to be filled before the detection can work

steps.description: Prototype the detection logic and test it against historical data.

outputs.name: prototype-detection
outputs.desc: Draft detection rule or query

outputs.name: historical-test-results
outputs.desc: Results from running the prototype against historical log data

process: Write the initial detection logic targeting the technique's observable artifacts
Run the prototype against historical data covering the last 30 to 90 days
Review matches to separate true positives from false positives
Iterate on the logic to reduce noise

steps.description: Measure the detection's true positive rate, false positive rate, and performance impact.

inputs.name: prototype-detection
inputs.desc: Detection rule or query to measure

outputs.name: detection-metrics
outputs.desc: True positive rate, false positive rate, and query performance

outputs.name: threshold-recommendations
outputs.desc: Recommended thresholds and tuning parameters

process: Calculate true positive rate against labeled attack data or red team exercises
Calculate false positive rate against normal business activity
Measure query execution time and resource consumption
Determine acceptable thresholds for production deployment

steps.description: Deploy the detection to production with proper monitoring and alert routing.

outputs.name: deployed-detection
outputs.desc: Detection rule deployed to the production SIEM

outputs.name: alert-routing-config
outputs.desc: Configuration for how alerts from this detection are routed and prioritized

process: Configure the detection rule in the production SIEM with the validated thresholds
Set up alert routing to the appropriate SOC tier based on severity
Create the analyst runbook for investigating alerts from this detection
Enable monitoring of the detection's performance metrics

steps.description: Produce the detection engineering report documenting the full lifecycle.

outputs.name: detection-report
outputs.desc: Full report covering gap analysis, design, testing, and deployment

outputs.name: coverage-map-update
outputs.desc: Updated ATT&CK coverage map reflecting the new detection

process: Document the coverage gap that motivated the detection
Record the detection logic, data sources, thresholds, and known limitations
Include test results and the analyst runbook for reference
Update the ATT&CK coverage map

description: Process threat intelligence from raw collection through analysis, production, and dissemination to stakeholders.

steps.description: Collect threat intelligence from feeds, reports, sharing communities, and internal sources.

inputs.name: intel-sources
inputs.desc: List of subscribed feeds, sharing groups, and report providers

outputs.name: raw-intel-collection
outputs.desc: Collected indicators, reports, and advisories in raw form

outputs.name: source-reliability-scores
outputs.desc: Reliability rating for each source based on historical accuracy

process: Pull indicators and reports from STIX/TAXII feeds and commercial providers
Collect human intelligence from sharing communities (ISACs, trusted groups)
Gather internal intelligence from incident investigations and threat hunts
Tag each item with source and collection timestamp

steps.description: Normalize collected intelligence into a standard format with consistent taxonomy.

inputs.name: raw-intel-collection
inputs.desc: Raw indicators and reports from multiple sources

outputs.name: normalized-intel
outputs.desc: Intelligence in standard format (STIX objects) with consistent naming

outputs.name: dedup-report
outputs.desc: Report of duplicate indicators merged and conflicting data resolved

process: Convert all indicators to a standard format (STIX 2.1 objects)
Apply consistent taxonomy for threat actors, malware families, and techniques
Deduplicate indicators from multiple sources and resolve conflicting metadata
Apply source reliability weighting

steps.description: Enrich normalized intelligence with internal context and additional external data.

outputs.name: enriched-intel
outputs.desc: Intelligence enriched with sighting data, asset context, and related indicators

outputs.name: internal-sightings
outputs.desc: Matches found in internal logs and historical incident data

process: Check indicators against internal logs for historical sightings
Enrich IP addresses and domains with WHOIS, geolocation, and reputation data
Link indicators to known campaigns, threat actors, and ATT&CK techniques
Flag any indicators that match assets or users in the environment

steps.description: Analyze enriched intelligence for relevance to the organization's specific risk profile.

inputs.name: enriched-intel
inputs.desc: Intelligence with internal context and enrichment

outputs.name: relevance-assessment
outputs.desc: Each intelligence item rated for relevance to the organization

outputs.name: priority-intel-items
outputs.desc: High-relevance items requiring immediate action or attention

process: Score each item by relevance: does it target our industry, technology, geography, or known partners
Weight by confidence: source reliability, corroboration from multiple sources, recency
Identify items requiring immediate action (active campaigns targeting our sector)
Deprioritize items with low relevance or confidence

steps.description: Produce finished intelligence products tailored to different stakeholder audiences.

outputs.name: intel-products
outputs.desc: Finished reports, bulletins, and indicator lists for stakeholders

outputs.name: detection-indicators
outputs.desc: Machine-readable indicators formatted for ingestion into security tools

process: Write executive summaries for leadership highlighting strategic threats
Produce tactical bulletins for the SOC with indicators and detection guidance
Format machine-readable indicator lists for SIEM and EDR ingestion
Create technical deep-dives for incident responders on priority threats

steps.description: Disseminate finished intelligence to stakeholders and feed indicators into detection systems.

outputs.name: dissemination-record
outputs.desc: Log of what was sent to whom and when

outputs.name: feedback-requests
outputs.desc: Requests for feedback on intelligence usefulness from recipients

process: Distribute reports to the appropriate stakeholder groups based on classification and relevance
Ingest indicators into the SIEM, EDR, and firewall block lists
Share relevant intelligence with trusted partners and ISACs per sharing agreements
Request feedback from recipients to improve future intelligence products

description: Investigate a confirmed security incident from scoping through root cause analysis and remediation recommendations.

steps.description: Scope the incident to determine affected systems, data, users, and timeframe.

inputs.name: incident-trigger
inputs.desc: Initial alert or report that triggered the investigation

inputs.name: initial-indicators
inputs.desc: Known indicators of compromise from the triggering event

outputs.name: incident-scope
outputs.desc: Defined scope: affected systems, users, data types, and time window

outputs.name: investigation-plan
outputs.desc: Plan for evidence collection and analysis priorities

process: Identify all systems that communicated with known malicious indicators
Determine which user accounts were involved or potentially compromised
Classify the data types at risk on affected systems
Define the investigation time window from earliest indicator to present

steps.description: Collect and preserve digital evidence from affected systems following forensic standards.

inputs.name: incident-scope
inputs.desc: Systems, users, and timeframe to investigate

outputs.name: evidence-inventory
outputs.desc: Catalog of all collected evidence with chain of custody records

outputs.name: preserved-artifacts
outputs.desc: Forensic images, log exports, and memory captures

process: Capture volatile evidence first: memory dumps, network connections, running processes
Export relevant logs from SIEM, EDR, authentication systems, and cloud audit trails
Create forensic disk images of affected systems where needed
Document the chain of custody for all collected evidence

steps.description: Analyze the collected evidence to reconstruct the full attack chain.

outputs.name: attack-chain-timeline
outputs.desc: Chronological reconstruction of the attacker's actions

outputs.name: attacker-ttps
outputs.desc: Techniques, tactics, and procedures used, mapped to ATT&CK

process: Build a timeline of events across all evidence sources
Identify the initial access vector and first compromise timestamp
Trace lateral movement, privilege escalation, and persistence mechanisms
Map each attacker action to the MITRE ATT&CK framework

steps.description: Identify the root cause and contributing factors that enabled the incident.

outputs.name: root-cause-analysis
outputs.desc: Root cause and contributing factors with evidence

outputs.name: control-failures
outputs.desc: Security controls that failed or were absent

process: Identify the vulnerability or weakness exploited for initial access
Determine why existing controls did not prevent or detect each stage
Distinguish between root cause (the exploited weakness) and contributing factors (detection gaps, delayed response)

steps.description: Determine the full extent of the compromise including data access, exfiltration, and persistence.

outputs.name: compromise-extent
outputs.desc: Full accounting of what was accessed, modified, or exfiltrated

outputs.name: persistence-inventory
outputs.desc: All persistence mechanisms installed by the attacker

process: Catalog all data the attacker accessed based on log evidence
Determine if data was exfiltrated by analyzing network traffic and data transfer logs
Identify all persistence mechanisms (backdoors, scheduled tasks, modified accounts)
Assess whether the attacker retains any access

steps.description: Recommend containment actions and long-term remediation based on investigation findings.

inputs.name: compromise-extent
inputs.desc: What was accessed, modified, or exfiltrated

outputs.name: containment-actions
outputs.desc: Immediate actions to stop the attack and prevent further damage

outputs.name: remediation-plan
outputs.desc: Long-term fixes addressing root cause and control failures

process: Define immediate containment: isolate systems, reset credentials, block indicators
Plan eradication: remove all persistence, rebuild compromised systems
Recommend long-term remediation: patch the root cause, improve failed controls
Prioritize actions by urgency and impact

steps.description: Produce the investigation report documenting the incident from detection through remediation.

outputs.name: investigation-report
outputs.desc: Complete incident investigation report

outputs.name: lessons-learned
outputs.desc: Lessons learned and improvements for future incident prevention and response

process: Write the executive summary: what happened, when, what was affected, and current status
Document the full technical analysis with timeline, TTPs, and evidence references
Include containment actions taken and remediation plan with owners and timelines
Capture lessons learned for process improvement

description: Build a security operations metrics program from metric definition through dashboard creation and reporting cadence.

steps.description: Define the key security operations metrics aligned with program objectives.

inputs.name: program-objectives
inputs.desc: Security program goals and stakeholder reporting requirements

inputs.name: available-data-sources
inputs.desc: Inventory of security tools, logs, and ticketing systems with available data

outputs.name: metric-definitions
outputs.desc: Each metric with name, formula, data source, and collection frequency

outputs.name: metric-priority-list
outputs.desc: Metrics ranked by importance for the initial dashboard

process: Define operational metrics: MTTD, MTTR, alert volume, false positive rate, escalation rate
Define coverage metrics: detection coverage by ATT&CK technique, vulnerability scan coverage, patch compliance
Define program metrics: risk reduction over time, incident trend, training completion
Rank by stakeholder need and data availability

steps.description: Map each metric to its data source and define the collection pipeline.

inputs.name: metric-definitions
inputs.desc: Metrics with formulas and data sources

outputs.name: data-pipeline-design
outputs.desc: Collection pipeline for each metric including source, extraction, and storage

outputs.name: data-gap-list
outputs.desc: Metrics that cannot be collected with current tooling

process: For each metric, identify the exact API, log query, or database table that provides the raw data
Design the extraction and transformation logic for each data source
Identify metrics that require data not currently collected and note the gap

steps.description: Build the automated collection pipeline that gathers metric data on schedule.

outputs.name: collection-pipeline
outputs.desc: Operational pipeline collecting metrics on the defined schedule

outputs.name: pipeline-test-results
outputs.desc: Validation that each metric collects correctly

process: Configure the data extraction for each source (API calls, log queries, ticketing exports)
Set up the transformation and storage layer
Test each metric's collection against known values
Set the collection schedule (hourly, daily, weekly depending on the metric)

steps.description: Create the dashboard visualizations for each metric with appropriate chart types.

outputs.name: dashboard-layout
outputs.desc: Dashboard with visualizations for each metric

outputs.name: drill-down-views
outputs.desc: Detailed views for investigating metric anomalies

process: Select the appropriate chart type for each metric (time series, gauge, bar, table)
Arrange the dashboard with the highest priority metrics in the primary view
Create drill-down views for each metric that allow investigation of anomalies
Apply consistent color coding for status (red, yellow, green thresholds)

steps.description: Establish baselines and targets for each metric based on initial data.

outputs.name: metric-baselines
outputs.desc: Baseline values for each metric established from initial collection period

outputs.name: metric-targets
outputs.desc: Target values and improvement timelines for each metric

process: Collect at least 30 days of data to establish statistical baselines
Set normal ranges and anomaly thresholds for each metric
Define improvement targets based on industry benchmarks and program goals

steps.description: Establish the reporting cadence and distribution for security metrics.

outputs.name: reporting-schedule
outputs.desc: Weekly, monthly, and quarterly reporting schedule with stakeholder distribution

outputs.name: metrics-program-document
outputs.desc: Complete documentation of the metrics program

process: Define the weekly operational review cadence for the SOC team
Set the monthly management report schedule with trend analysis
Plan quarterly executive reviews with strategic metrics and improvement progress
Document the full metrics program: definitions, baselines, targets, and reporting schedule

description: Run a vulnerability management cycle from scanning through remediation tracking and risk reduction reporting.

steps.description: Scan the environment for vulnerabilities across network, application, and container assets.

inputs.name: scan-scope
inputs.desc: IP ranges, applications, and container registries to scan

inputs.name: scan-credentials
inputs.desc: Authenticated scan credentials for each target type

outputs.name: raw-scan-results
outputs.desc: Vulnerability findings from all scanners

outputs.name: scan-coverage-report
outputs.desc: Percentage of assets successfully scanned with any gaps noted

process: Run network vulnerability scans against the defined IP ranges
Run application scans (DAST) against web applications in the scope
Scan container images in registries for known CVEs
Record coverage: which assets were scanned, which failed, and why

steps.description: Prioritize vulnerabilities by exploitability, asset criticality, and business context.

outputs.name: prioritized-vulns
outputs.desc: Vulnerabilities ranked by risk: exploitability, asset criticality, exposure

outputs.name: priority-methodology
outputs.desc: Documentation of the prioritization criteria and weights used

process: Score each vulnerability using CVSS base score, EPSS exploitability probability, and known exploit availability
Weight by asset criticality (crown jewels, internet-facing, internal, development)
Factor in network exposure: internet-facing assets receive higher priority than segmented internal systems
Produce the ranked list with risk justification for each item

steps.description: Assign remediation owners and deadlines for prioritized vulnerabilities.

inputs.name: prioritized-vulns
inputs.desc: Ranked vulnerability list with risk scores

outputs.name: remediation-assignments
outputs.desc: Each vulnerability assigned to an owner with a deadline based on severity

outputs.name: remediation-tickets
outputs.desc: Tickets created in the tracking system for each assignment

process: Map each vulnerability to the responsible team based on asset ownership
Set remediation deadlines by severity: critical 7 days, high 30 days, medium 90 days, low 180 days
Create tracking tickets with vulnerability details, remediation guidance, and deadline

steps.description: Track remediation progress and follow up on overdue items.

inputs.name: remediation-assignments
inputs.desc: Assigned vulnerabilities with owners and deadlines

outputs.name: progress-report
outputs.desc: Status of all remediation efforts: completed, in progress, overdue

outputs.name: escalation-list
outputs.desc: Overdue items requiring management escalation

process: Query the ticketing system for remediation status updates
Calculate on-time vs overdue rates by team and severity
Generate the escalation list for items past their deadline with no progress
Send reminders and escalation notifications

steps.description: Verify that remediated vulnerabilities are actually fixed by rescanning.

outputs.name: verification-results
outputs.desc: Rescan results confirming fix or identifying regression

outputs.name: reopen-list
outputs.desc: Items that failed verification and need to be reopened

process: Rescan assets where vulnerabilities were reported as fixed
Compare new scan results against the original findings
Confirm each fix or identify regressions and incomplete remediations
Reopen tickets for failed verifications

steps.description: Report on overall risk reduction from the vulnerability management cycle.

outputs.name: vuln-management-report
outputs.desc: Full cycle report with findings, remediation rates, and risk reduction

outputs.name: risk-trend-data
outputs.desc: Trend data showing risk reduction over time across scan cycles

process: Calculate the overall remediation rate and average time to remediate by severity
Compute risk reduction: total risk score at scan vs total remaining risk
Compare against previous cycles to show trend
Highlight persistent risks and recommend process improvements

description: Build a SOAR playbook for automated security response from use case selection through deployment and measurement.

steps.description: Select the use case for automation based on alert volume, response time, and analyst effort.

inputs.name: alert-statistics
inputs.desc: Alert volume, response time, and analyst hours per alert type

inputs.name: existing-playbooks
inputs.desc: List of already automated use cases to avoid duplication

outputs.name: selected-use-case
outputs.desc: The use case to automate with justification based on volume and effort

outputs.name: manual-workflow-doc
outputs.desc: Current manual investigation steps for this alert type

process: Rank alert types by the product of volume and average analyst time per alert
Exclude use cases already automated or requiring complex judgment
Select the highest-value candidate that can be meaningfully automated
Document the current manual workflow step by step

steps.description: Design the automated workflow including enrichment, decision logic, and response actions.

outputs.name: workflow-design
outputs.desc: Automated workflow diagram with enrichment, decision, and action steps

outputs.name: integration-requirements
outputs.desc: APIs and tools the playbook needs to connect to

process: Map each manual step to an automated equivalent (API call, lookup, comparison)
Define decision points: what conditions trigger automated containment vs analyst review
Identify all tool integrations needed (SIEM, EDR, firewall, ticketing, email)
Design the notification and escalation paths for cases requiring human judgment

steps.description: Implement the playbook in the SOAR platform with all integrations and logic.

outputs.name: implemented-playbook
outputs.desc: Working playbook in the SOAR platform

outputs.name: integration-test-results
outputs.desc: Results of testing each integration point

process: Configure each integration with the required API credentials and permissions
Build the workflow steps: trigger, enrichment queries, decision logic, actions
Test each integration point individually to verify connectivity and data flow
Set error handling: what happens when an integration fails or returns unexpected data

steps.description: Test the playbook with simulated alerts to verify correct behavior.

inputs.name: implemented-playbook
inputs.desc: Working playbook in the SOAR platform

outputs.name: simulation-results
outputs.desc: Results of running simulated true positive and false positive alerts

outputs.name: edge-case-notes
outputs.desc: Edge cases discovered during testing and how they were handled

process: Run simulated true positive alerts through the playbook and verify correct containment
Run simulated false positive alerts and verify no incorrect actions taken
Test edge cases: missing data, slow API responses, ambiguous indicators
Verify analyst notifications and escalations work correctly

steps.description: Measure the time and effort savings from automation compared to the manual process.

outputs.name: time-savings-analysis
outputs.desc: Comparison of manual vs automated response time and analyst effort

outputs.name: roi-calculation
outputs.desc: Return on investment in analyst hours saved per month

process: Compare automated response time against the historical manual average
Calculate analyst hours saved per alert and project monthly savings based on volume
Identify remaining manual steps and their time cost
Compute the ROI: analyst hours saved minus the time spent building and maintaining the playbook

steps.description: Produce the playbook documentation including workflow, integrations, and maintenance procedures.

outputs.name: playbook-documentation
outputs.desc: Complete documentation: workflow diagram, integrations, decision logic, maintenance

outputs.name: maintenance-schedule
outputs.desc: Schedule for reviewing and updating the playbook

process: Document the workflow with decision logic, integrations, and error handling
Write the analyst guide for handling escalated cases from this playbook
Define the maintenance schedule: quarterly review, integration health checks, metric review
Record the ROI and time savings for program reporting
